2026-11-04 pediatric HAE primary appraisal: consider HAE with recurrent unexplained swelling/abdominal attacks even without family history; obtain C4 and antigenic/functional C1INH,with confirmatory testing and age-aware infant interpretation. Treat airway/facial/neck attacks promptly; airway involvement requires emergency hospital referral with airway capability. Bradykinin attacks differ from anaphylaxis,but diagnostic uncertainty must not delay indicated anaphylaxis care. Age-specific options and approvals differ between Europe and the US. Ecallantide has anaphylaxis risk; recombinant C1INH has unestablished laryngeal efficacy. Rescue medication remains necessary despite prophylaxis. Procedure prophylaxis does not replace acute rescue availability. Recommendations report evidence levels/consensus agreement,not interchangeable universal GRADE strength. These selected primary passages advance review; no article or comprehensive full-guideline appraisal asserted.

2026-11-04 medication-table verification: publisher Table4 lists sebetralstat≥12years,300mg tablet; do not interpret tablet strength as the usual dose.
